newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM may list crude basket as first oil contract.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM may list crude basket as first oil contract.

text.p: The Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) said on Tuesday it may list a basket of Middle Eastern and regional crude grades instead of North Sea Brent or West Texas Intermediate (WTI) as its first oil futures contract.

"After my trip to the London and Singapore exchanges, a basket of crudes seems to be a better choice for us rather than listing Brent or WTI," Mitsuhiro Onosato, general manager of TOCOM's planning department, told Reuters.

Onosato visited London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) and the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) in June to exchange information on TOCOM's plan to list an energy futures contract.

At the meeting in London, IPE officials said they were reluctant to cooperate with TOCOM on listing a Brent blend futures contract, as it is already traded on SIMEX, whose trading hours largely overlap with TOCOM's, Onosato said.
SIMEX has a mutual offset agreement with the IPE. With a mutual offset accord, positions opened on SIMEX can be closed on the IPE and vice versa.

Since there is only minimal support among Asian traders to list WTI, which has little bearing on Asian oil market fundamentals, listing a basket of Middle Eastern and Asian crudes might be the best option at the moment, Onosato said.
TOCOM has yet to discuss which crude grades should be included in a possible basket.
Tentative plans on the listing of an energy futures contract, including contract specifications and the timing, should be complied by the autumn.

TOCOM said in May it planned to list either crude oil or gasoline in 1999 as its first-ever energy futures contract, and that if crude oil were to be listed, global benchmarks Brent or WTI were likely choices.
A decision on whether crude oil or gasoline will be listed has not been reached, Onosato said.
